## Why

Each place's Google Maps link ends in a long tracking parameter, such as `https://maps.google.com/?cid=8720190008484083912&g_mp=Cidnb29nbGUubWFwcy5wbGFjZXMudjEuUGxhY2VzLlNlYXJjaFRleHQQAhgEIAA`. The `g_mp` part is about 70 characters, and the link works without it. Every search result and `read_place` reply shows the link, so a `search_along_leg` reply of 20 places carries about 1,400 characters of it. Found in PR #159, while checking the place searches against Google.

## Design

- [Google design](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/data-sources/google.md), section 2.2 (`googleMapsUri`).

## Open questions

- Drop the `g_mp` parameter when a place is parsed, so it's never stored, or only when a tool shows the link? Places stored before the change would keep it.
- Is it worth doing at all? It's tokens in the workers' context, not a bug.
- Should the search replies be trimmed more widely? A real `search_along_leg` reply of 20 places ran to about 19,000 characters, and `search_near`'s 10 places to about 10,000 (PR #159). The leg scout may run several queries per leg, so this adds up in its context. Each place carries Google's summaries, its hours, and two links, and the summaries are likely the largest part. Look at which fields help a worker choose, and cut the rest. Best judged once the stay researcher (#60) and the leg scout (#61) exist, so their real use shows what they read. Added on 2026-10-26.

## Do

- Decide, and if it's worth it, drop the parameter from the links the agents see.

## Done when

- A search's reply shows each Google Maps link without `g_mp`, and the link still opens the place.

## Ends in

A PR, or a decision not to.

**Settled in:** chat.
